chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the father and the grandfather give in marriage, the marriage is valid for the first one. So if they are both in one situation, the grandfather is more entitled.
ai.seo_question: Who has the higher priority in marriage guardianship: the father or the grandfather?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the hierarchy of marital guardianship (wilayah al-tajfiz) in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the father over the grandfather under normal circumstances. However, it introduces a nuanced exception where simultaneous action grants precedence to the grandfather, reflecting the scholarly debate on whether proximity of lineage or seniority in the direct male line takes precedence when both parties act concurrently. This ruling is foundational for understanding the legal mechanics of marriage contracts in the absence of the woman's explicit consent.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Hisham Bin Salim, and Muhammad Bin Hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the father and the grand-father gives in marriage, the (valid) marriage would be of the first one. So if it was together, in one situation, so the grand-father is higher’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Flakim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If both father and grandfather give in marriage, the first one’s marriage is effective and if both happens at the same time, the grandfather has the priority.’”
